The [Reading](reading.qmd) page indexes papers. This page indexes everything
else: software that can be executed, courses that can be enrolled in, regulatory
guidance that specifies what a deliverable must contain, repositories from which
a runnable model or a real dataset can be obtained, and databases consulted for
a fact about a drug.

The source of truth is [`resources.csv`](https://github.com/mgl0619/modelers-bench/blob/main/resources.csv),
one row per resource, validated by `scripts/check_resources.py`. This page is
generated from it. To add a resource, add a row and open a pull request.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Provenance, and the limits of it

**Every URL below was retrieved and confirmed before its row was written**, and
the `cost` and `licence` fields were read from the page rather than recalled.
This matters most where the answer is counterintuitive: Open Systems Pharmacology
is free for commercial use, KEGG states explicitly that it is not a public
database, and DrugBank requires a licence for any redistribution of its content.

This procedure does **not** establish that a link remains live, that a price is
unchanged, or that a description is correct about something the page did not
state. Where a page was silent, the field records `unknown` rather than an
inference. The number of `unknown` licences here is higher than is comfortable;
each is a gap in the record, not a formatting convention.

Errors are bugs. Open an issue.
:::

## Two facets, and why most rows are `any`

Beyond category and domain, each row carries a **modality** and a **therapeutic
area**. Both default to `any`, and that default is the majority value for a
defensible reason: an ODE solver does not know what molecule it is integrating.
Tagging `nlmixr2` as *oncology* would not make the database more useful, it
would make a filtered view actively wrong.

So a row is tagged only where it is genuinely specialised — a guidance that
governs one modality, a model built for one disease, a dataset from one
indication. The consequence is that filtering by modality or disease returns a
**small, dense set**, which is the intent.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import csv, html, json, collections
from pathlib import Path

rows = list(csv.DictReader(Path("resources.csv").open(encoding="utf-8", newline="")))

MOD_ORDER = ["small-molecule", "peptide", "protein-mab", "adc", "bispecific",
             "oligonucleotide", "cell-therapy", "gene-therapy", "vaccine",
             "radioligand"]
MOD_LABEL = {"small-molecule": "small molecule", "peptide": "peptide",
             "protein-mab": "mAb / Fc-fusion", "adc": "ADC",
             "bispecific": "bispecific / TCE", "oligonucleotide": "oligonucleotide",
             "cell-therapy": "cell therapy", "gene-therapy": "gene therapy",
             "vaccine": "vaccine", "radioligand": "radioligand", "any": "any"}
DIS_ORDER = ["oncology", "immunology", "infectious-disease", "cns",
             "cardiometabolic", "respiratory", "hepatology", "nephrology",
             "haematology", "rare-disease"]
DIS_LABEL = {"oncology": "oncology", "immunology": "immunology",
             "infectious-disease": "infectious disease", "cns": "CNS",
             "cardiometabolic": "cardiometabolic", "respiratory": "respiratory",
             "hepatology": "hepatology", "nephrology": "nephrology",
             "haematology": "haematology", "rare-disease": "rare disease",
             "any": "any"}

def runnable(r):
    return (r["category"] == "software"
            or (r["category"] == "repository"
                and r["subcategory"] in ("model repository", "QSP", "reproducibility")))

print("### Where the field's tooling actually sits\n")
print("Counting rows by modality against what kind of resource they are. "
      "This is a census of this database, not of the world — but the database "
      "was assembled by searching each modality deliberately, so the shape is "
      "informative.\n")
print("| Modality | Regulatory guidance | Runnable models / tools | Datasets | Reference |")
print("|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|")
gaps = []
for m in MOD_ORDER:
    sel = [r for r in rows if m in r["modality"].split("|")]
    g = sum(1 for r in sel if r["category"] == "guidance")
    run = sum(1 for r in sel if runnable(r))
    d = sum(1 for r in sel if r["category"] == "repository" and r["subcategory"] == "dataset")
    ref = sum(1 for r in sel if r["category"] == "reference")
    mark = " **←**" if (g > 0 and run == 0) else ""
    if g > 0 and run == 0:
        gaps.append((MOD_LABEL[m], g))
    print(f"| {MOD_LABEL[m]} | {g} | {run}{mark} | {d} | {ref} |")

if gaps:
    names = " and ".join(f"**{n}** ({g} guidance documents)" for n, g in gaps)
    print(f"\nThe marked rows are the finding. For {names}, **no** runnable, "
          f"openly licensed quantitative model could be located and verified at "
          f"all. Regulators have specified what these modalities must "
          f"demonstrate before the open modelling community has produced "
          f"anything to demonstrate it with. That asymmetry is not a gap in "
          f"this database so much as a gap in the field — and it marks where a "
          f"motivated modeller could contribute something that does not "
          f"currently exist.\n")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What was searched for and not found

Three modality-specific searches returned nothing open and runnable, and the
absence is recorded here rather than quietly omitted:

- **Gene therapy and AAV pharmacokinetics.** Every public repository located was
  capsid engineering, sequencing analysis or vector quality control. No open
  vector biodistribution, transduction or transgene-expression PK model was
  found. ICH S12 specifies how to run the biodistribution studies; nothing open
  exists to model their output.
- **Oligonucleotide PK/PD.** Published GalNAc-siRNA and antisense PBPK models
  have no accompanying public code, and the open oligonucleotide repositories on
  GitHub are sequence-design tools. FDA finalised clinical pharmacology guidance
  for this modality in June 2024.
- **Immunogenicity and anti-drug antibody PK/PD.** Assay guidance and data
  standards are abundant; an open implementation of an ADA-mediated clearance
  model is not. This is conspicuous given that ADA is a routine covariate in
  biologics population PK.

Respiratory disease progression was searched and produced one qualified
biomarker (plasma fibrinogen in COPD, inside the EMA qualification catalogue) and
no obtainable model.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import csv, html, json
from pathlib import Path

rows = list(csv.DictReader(Path("resources.csv").open(encoding="utf-8", newline="")))

CATEGORY_ORDER = ["guidance", "software", "repository", "reference", "course"]
CATEGORY_LABEL = {
    "guidance":   "Regulatory guidance",
    "software":   "Software and packages",
    "repository": "Model repositories and datasets",
    "reference":  "Reference databases",
    "course":     "Courses, training and societies",
}
CATEGORY_BLURB = {
    "guidance":   "Free, public, and mostly short. These state what a submitted "
                  "analysis must contain, which makes them the most precise "
                  "available specification of the work.",
    "software":   "Read the cost column first. Population PK can be done "
                  "entirely without licence fees; PBPK could not, until Open "
                  "Systems Pharmacology.",
    "repository": "Sources from which a runnable model or a real dataset can be "
                  "obtained. Where access requires an application rather than a "
                  "download, the note says so.",
    "reference":  "Lookup resources. The licence column governs whether anything "
                  "found here may be reproduced in your own work.",
    "course":     "Ordered so that material requiring neither budget nor "
                  "institutional affiliation appears first.",
}
COST_LABEL = {"free": "free", "free-academic": "free for academics",
              "freemium": "free tier", "commercial": "paid",
              "unknown": "cost unstated"}
DOMAIN_LABEL = {"pharmacology": "pharmacology", "pkpd": "PK/PD", "poppk": "PopPK",
                "pbpk": "PBPK", "qsp": "QSP", "stats-ml": "stats & ML",
                "regulatory": "regulatory", "general": "general"}
MOD_LABEL = {"small-molecule": "small molecule", "peptide": "peptide",
             "protein-mab": "mAb / Fc-fusion", "adc": "ADC",
             "bispecific": "bispecific / TCE", "oligonucleotide": "oligonucleotide",
             "cell-therapy": "cell therapy", "gene-therapy": "gene therapy",
             "vaccine": "vaccine", "radioligand": "radioligand"}
DIS_LABEL = {"oncology": "oncology", "immunology": "immunology",
             "infectious-disease": "infectious disease", "cns": "CNS",
             "cardiometabolic": "cardiometabolic", "respiratory": "respiratory",
             "hepatology": "hepatology", "nephrology": "nephrology",
             "haematology": "haematology", "rare-disease": "rare disease"}

n_free = sum(1 for r in rows if r["cost"] in ("free", "free-academic"))
verified = sorted({r["verified"] for r in rows})[-1]

print(f"## The database\n")
print(f"**{len(rows)} resources**, of which **{n_free}** are usable at no cost. "
      f"Links last verified {verified}.\n")

print("""
<div class="res-controls">
  <input type="search" id="res-q" placeholder="Search name, description, maintainer…" aria-label="Search resources">
  <label class="res-freeonly"><input type="checkbox" id="res-free"> free only</label>
  <span class="res-count" id="res-count"></span>
  <div class="res-facet"><span class="res-facet-l">domain</span><span class="res-chips" id="res-domains"></span></div>
  <div class="res-facet"><span class="res-facet-l">modality</span><span class="res-chips" id="res-modality"></span></div>
  <div class="res-facet"><span class="res-facet-l">disease</span><span class="res-chips" id="res-disease"></span></div>
</div>
""")

def esc(s):
    return html.escape(s or "")

for cat in CATEGORY_ORDER:
    group = [r for r in rows if r["category"] == cat]
    if not group:
        continue
    print(f'\n<h3 class="res-h" data-cat="{cat}">{CATEGORY_LABEL[cat]} '
          f'<span class="res-n">{len(group)}</span></h3>')
    print(f'<p class="res-blurb">{esc(CATEGORY_BLURB[cat])}</p>')

    subs = []
    for r in group:
        if r["subcategory"] not in subs:
            subs.append(r["subcategory"])

    for sub in subs:
        items = [r for r in group if r["subcategory"] == sub]
        print(f'<h4 class="res-sub">{esc(sub)}</h4>')
        print('<div class="res-list">')
        for r in items:
            doms = r["domains"].split("|")
            mods = [m for m in r["modality"].split("|") if m != "any"]
            diss = [d for d in r["disease"].split("|") if d != "any"]
            blob = " ".join([r["name"], r["description"], r["best_for"],
                             r["maintainer"], r["notes"], r["licence"]]).lower()
            free = "1" if r["cost"] in ("free", "free-academic") else "0"
            tags = "".join(f'<span class="res-dom">{DOMAIN_LABEL.get(d, d)}</span>' for d in doms)
            tags += "".join(f'<span class="res-mod">{MOD_LABEL.get(m, m)}</span>' for m in mods)
            tags += "".join(f'<span class="res-dis">{DIS_LABEL.get(d, d)}</span>' for d in diss)
            lang = f' &middot; {esc(r["language"])}' if r["language"] not in ("n/a", "") else ""
            note = f'<p class="res-note">{esc(r["notes"])}</p>' if r["notes"] else ""
            # Emitted as ONE line, deliberately. Quarto runs this output
            # through Pandoc as markdown, and a line indented four spaces
            # inside a raw HTML block becomes an indented code block - which
            # is exactly what happened to the anchor and cost badge here
            # before. Keeping each card on a single line means Pandoc passes
            # it through untouched, with no injected <pre> and no stray <p>
            # wrappers that would break the flex layout in .res-head.
            card = (
                f'<div class="res-item" data-domains="{esc(r["domains"])}"'
                f' data-modality="{esc(r["modality"])}"'
                f' data-disease="{esc(r["disease"])}"'
                f' data-free="{free}" data-blob="{esc(blob)}">'
                f'<div class="res-head">'
                f'<a class="res-name" href="{esc(r["url"])}" target="_blank"'
                f' rel="noopener">{esc(r["name"])}</a>'
                f'<span class="res-cost res-cost-{esc(r["cost"])}">'
                f'{esc(COST_LABEL[r["cost"]])}</span>'
                f'</div>'
                f'<div class="res-meta">{esc(r["maintainer"])}{lang}'
                f' &middot; <span class="res-lic">{esc(r["licence"])}</span></div>'
                f'<p class="res-desc">{esc(r["description"])}</p>'
                f'<p class="res-use"><strong>Use it for:</strong>'
                f' {esc(r["best_for"])}</p>'
                f'{note}'
                f'<div class="res-doms">{tags}</div>'
                f'</div>'
            )
            print(card)
        print('</div>')

print("\n<script>")
print(f"window.RES_LABELS = {json.dumps({'domains': DOMAIN_LABEL, 'modality': MOD_LABEL, 'disease': DIS_LABEL})};")
print("</script>")
```

<script>
(function(){
  var items=[].slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('.res-item'));
  if(!items.length) return;
  var q=document.getElementById('res-q'),
      freeBox=document.getElementById('res-free'),
      countEl=document.getElementById('res-count'),
      L=window.RES_LABELS||{},
      facets=[
        {key:'domains', box:document.getElementById('res-domains'), active:new Set()},
        {key:'modality',box:document.getElementById('res-modality'),active:new Set()},
        {key:'disease', box:document.getElementById('res-disease'), active:new Set()}
      ];

  facets.forEach(function(f){
    if(!f.box) return;
    var present=[];
    items.forEach(function(el){
      el.dataset[f.key].split('|').forEach(function(v){
        if(v!=='any' && present.indexOf(v)<0) present.push(v);
      });
    });
    var labels=L[f.key]||{};
    // keep the declared label order where we have one, else alphabetical
    var order=Object.keys(labels);
    present.sort(function(a,b){
      var ia=order.indexOf(a), ib=order.indexOf(b);
      if(ia<0&&ib<0) return a<b?-1:1;
      if(ia<0) return 1; if(ib<0) return -1; return ia-ib;
    });
    present.forEach(function(v){
      var b=document.createElement('button');
      b.className='res-chip'; b.type='button';
      b.textContent=labels[v]||v;
      b.setAttribute('aria-pressed','false');
      b.addEventListener('click',function(){
        if(f.active.has(v)){f.active.delete(v);b.setAttribute('aria-pressed','false');}
        else{f.active.add(v);b.setAttribute('aria-pressed','true');}
        apply();
      });
      f.box.appendChild(b);
    });
  });

  function apply(){
    var term=(q.value||'').trim().toLowerCase(),
        onlyFree=freeBox.checked, shown=0;
    items.forEach(function(el){
      var ok=true;
      if(term && el.dataset.blob.indexOf(term)<0) ok=false;
      if(ok && onlyFree && el.dataset.free!=='1') ok=false;
      // facets combine as AND across facets, OR within a facet.
      // A row tagged `any` is deliberately EXCLUDED when a specific value is
      // selected: asking for "cell therapy" should not return every ODE solver.
      if(ok) facets.forEach(function(f){
        if(!ok || !f.active.size) return;
        var vals=el.dataset[f.key].split('|'), hit=false;
        f.active.forEach(function(v){ if(vals.indexOf(v)>=0) hit=true; });
        if(!hit) ok=false;
      });
      el.hidden=!ok; if(ok) shown++;
    });
    [].slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('.res-list')).forEach(function(list){
      var any=[].slice.call(list.querySelectorAll('.res-item')).some(function(e){return !e.hidden;});
      list.style.display=any?'':'none';
      var h=list.previousElementSibling;
      if(h&&h.classList.contains('res-sub')) h.style.display=any?'':'none';
    });
    [].slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('.res-h')).forEach(function(h){
      var n=h, anyLeft=false;
      while((n=n.nextElementSibling) && !n.classList.contains('res-h')){
        if(n.classList.contains('res-list') && n.style.display!=='none') anyLeft=true;
      }
      h.style.display=anyLeft?'':'none';
      var blurb=h.nextElementSibling;
      if(blurb&&blurb.classList.contains('res-blurb')) blurb.style.display=anyLeft?'':'none';
    });
    countEl.textContent=shown+' of '+items.length+' shown';
  }
  q.addEventListener('input',apply);
  freeBox.addEventListener('change',apply);
  apply();
})();
</script>

## Where these are used in the curriculum

| Page | What it draws on |
|---|---|
| [S0-00 · What quantitative pharmacology is](lessons/s0-00-what-is-qp/index.qmd) | The free courses from which a twelve-month self-study route can be assembled |
| [S0-03 · Data assembly](lessons/s0-03-data-assembly/index.qmd) | Datasets to work on once `CASE-SM` has taught what it can |
| [S0-04 · Choosing a stack](lessons/s0-04-choosing-a-stack/index.qmd) | The software table, priced, with free and paid alternatives set side by side |
| [S0-06 · Reading a model report](lessons/s0-06-reading-a-model-report/index.qmd) | FDA, EMA and ICH M15 — the review criteria written by those who review |
| [Strand P · Pharmacology](pharmacology.qmd) | Lecture courses, target databases, label archives and PBPK parameter sources |
| [Cases](cases.qmd) | Model repositories, and the modality-specific models `CASE-MAB` and `CASE-CELL` will build on |

## Exclusions

- **Anything that could not be retrieved.** Roughly thirty candidates were
  dropped for a failed fetch, a redirect to unrelated content, or a page that
  returned only a JavaScript shell. Several are real resources that could not be
  verified from their own page — PharmGKB and the Therapeutic Target Database
  among them — and they are omitted rather than described from memory.
- **Consortia presented as models.** The distinction between an organisation
  that has built a model and a model that can be obtained is recorded in the
  `notes` field throughout. C-Path's paediatric IBD coalition is listed with the
  explicit statement that nothing is available yet; the Alzheimer's trial
  simulation tool is listed with the statement that its application is under
  construction.
- **Anything defunct presented as current.** The DDMoRe Model Repository is
  included because its models remain downloadable, and its row states that every
  date signal on the site stops in 2018.
- **Textbooks.** Rowland & Tozer, Gabrielsson & Weiner and Rang & Dale are each
  worth owning. None has a canonical free page to link.
- **Prices, mostly.** Few vendors publish them. Where a page stated a figure the
  row records it; elsewhere it records that pricing is not published, which is
  itself informative.
